title: A phase-invariant thermal hydrogen screen permits deeper relative dips than a bare-star emission bound
abstract: We derive exact continuum dip bounds for an isothermal hydrogen screen with Thomson removal and thermal free-free transfer. Density can vary along each ray. A screen can emit both during and outside transit, so a bare-star emission bound cannot be used as an unresolved transit limit. At 0.8 micrometre, with gas at 10,000 K, brightness temperature 3,200 K, path 2.0871e11 cm and Gaunt factor one, the bare-star deficit is at most 0.7312%, but the unresolved dip can reach 9.0312%. That construction emits 1.1157 times the bare-star flux outside transit. We derive a dual bound with an independent emission cap. A cap of 1% limits the dip to 1.6948% for full coverage or 0.5432% for 10% coverage. Profiles attain these values in the transfer model. Exact layer transfer and independent transmission and emission integrations check the proof. These are conditional model results, not measurements of CPV stars. Phase-dependent scattering, cloud orientation changes, other gas opacities, realistic stellar spectra and physical support are excluded. The result gives a continuum test and shows why thermal emission alone does not reject gas dips. Code, synthetic results, source hashes and reproduction steps are included.

display.caption: Exact limits for a stated thermal hydrogen screen. The reference outside transit includes cloud emission. Wavelength maxima are separate optimizations, not one cloud spectrum.
